defects.quote: `δ_t = r_t + gamma · V(s_{t+1}) · (1 − terminated_t) − V(s_t)`, `A_t = δ_t + gamma · lam · (1 − terminated_t) · A_{t+1}`
defects.evidence: PPO rollouts are `rollout_steps` = 2048 agent-steps, and tank games are truncated at 1,000 steps. A rollout therefore crosses truncated game ends. gae only knows `terminated`, so across a truncation it chains A_{t+1} from the next game's first step and bootstraps from the next game's first value instead of the truncated state's value. That is wrong GAE. AD-03 promises that "learning targets bootstrap correctly on truncation".
defects.fix: Add a `truncated: np.ndarray` argument, or state that PPOAgent calls gae once per game segment with that segment's own bootstrap value. Add the invariant: "at a truncated step, δ uses V(s_T) of the truncated state and A_{t+1} is not carried across". Add a TC-42 case with a truncation in mid-rollout.

defects.quote: The hand-written PPO and the reference differ only in code, not settings
defects.evidence: AD-10 gives the reference a "Box action `(2,)` in [−1, 1]". Stable-Baselines3 PPO clips each sampled action to the Box bounds per axis before `env.step`. AD-11 says the hand-written agent's "Actions are sampled unclipped; the tank shortens them". The two policies therefore send different swim vectors for the same sample: (2, 0.5) becomes direction (0.89, 0.45) for the reference and (0.97, 0.24) for the hand-written agent. A REF-02 gap could come from action handling rather than code. AD-15's predator reference has the same problem.
defects.fix: In AD-10/AD-11 choose one action pipeline for both. Either the adapter's Box is unbounded (low=-inf, high=inf) so the tank alone shortens, or the hand-written agent applies the same per-axis clip to [−1, 1] before the tank. Record the choice in AD-11's Consequences and in M2's reference-mapping test.

defects.quote: each player's scores are pooled across its 5 training seeds
defects.evidence: EVAL-01 and run_claims pool 1,000 games (5 training seeds × 200) and test them as independent samples (TC-21: "games pooled across seeds"). For agent-vs-agent claims (PPO vs REINFORCE, hand-written vs reference, rung 3 vs rung 2), the main variance is between training seeds. Pooling games treats 5 runs as 1,000 replicates, so "significant" overstates the evidence about the learning algorithm.
defects.fix: In run_claims (and the EVAL-01/EVAL-08/EVAL-10/REF-03 wording), have the skill test at the training-seed level for comparisons between learners (e.g. a permutation or hierarchical test over the 5 per-seed means, or a test that respects seed blocks). Or state explicitly that the claims are conditional on these 5 trained runs. Add a known-answer case where the between-seed variance dominates.

defects.quote: The correction covers every spec in one call.
defects.evidence: For `not_worse` claims a pass means the "worse" test is not significant (compare.Claim). Applying a family-wide multiplicity correction to those tests raises their corrected p-values. So the more claims a report holds, the easier EVAL-03 and REF-03 pass. The correction is anti-conservative for exactly the claims it is meant to guard.
defects.fix: State in run_claims and compare.Claim that the multiplicity correction applies only to `greater` claims. `not_worse` claims are tested uncorrected at α, or corrected in the conservative direction, e.g. Bonferroni-tightened, which makes the worse-test easier to reject. Add a TC-23 variant with many claims in the family.

defects.quote: 8 pellets are present again from step 21
defects.evidence: Pellets and prey use different respawn counting. In TC-51 a pellet eaten at step 1 is back at step 21 (absent for steps 2–20, 19 steps), though HUNT-03 says "20 steps later". In TC-52 a prey caught at step 11 is back at step 62 (absent for steps 12–61, the full 50). A builder writing one shared respawn timer can't satisfy both.
defects.fix: Pick one convention and apply it to both. If absence is counted as in TC-52, change TC-51 to "8 pellets are present again from step 22". Otherwise change TC-52 to "stays done through step 60, and from step 61...". State the convention once in HUNT-03 and HUNT-04.

defects.quote: - A fish-tank rung with 8 fixed swim directions played by a value learner.
defects.evidence: Turn 19: "Your lean (1 + 3 + 4, with variation 2 optional) is fine." The idea doc lists this rung as "An optional rung 0 (8 fixed directions, played by the S1 value learner)". The spec moves it from optional to out of scope, a change the developer didn't make in their own words.
defects.fix: Ask the developer whether it should stay an optional rung (e.g. an optional, unscored PG rung 0 settings file) or be dropped. Then either remove this out-of-scope line or record the drop in the spec changelog as the developer's decision.

defects.quote: the real 5-seed runs pass TC-15, TC-16, TC-26 and TC-27
defects.evidence: TC-15 isn't a real 5-seed run. It is a synthetic 2,000-step corridor determinism case ("steps 2,000... seed 0, trained twice") that M1-T21 checks. plan.md's Exit has the same wording: "the real 5-seed ladder and reference runs pass TC-15, TC-16, TC-26 and TC-27".
defects.fix: In both roadmap.md M1 Exit and plan.md Scope Exit, move TC-15 into the synthetic list: "TC-01–TC-25 and TC-28 pass (including TC-15); the real 5-seed runs pass TC-16, TC-26 and TC-27 within QR-01–QR-05".

defects.evidence: M1-T31's acceptance runs "All five smoke commands" and requires "TC-01–TC-28 pass" (CORE-06). Its packet has neither PL-03 nor PL-05 (the eval and replay triggers), nor the TC-01–TC-28 sections.
defects.fix: Add PL-03, PL-05 and CORE-06 to M1-T31's Read line, or reword the acceptance to "the five smoke commands listed under Verify".

defects.quote: clips the policy's change to within 0.2 of its previous probability ratio
defects.evidence: PPO clips the new-to-old probability ratio to [1 − 0.2, 1 + 0.2], i.e. within 0.2 of 1. It doesn't clip against a "previous probability ratio". The example and TC-43 use the correct form.
defects.fix: Change to "...with an objective that clips the new-to-old probability ratio to between 0.8 and 1.2".
